extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and practitioners (attorneys/agents) filing USPTO Track One prioritized examination requests
extracted.subtask_description: Certification and request form to obtain prioritized examination (Track One) under 37 CFR 1.102(e), describing eligibility, required fees, claim limits, filing-route and oath requirements, RCE-specific conditions, signature rules, and Privacy Act disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment of required fees
rubrics_metrics.description: The processing fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(i), the prioritized examination fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(c), and if not already paid, the publication fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.18(d) have been filed with the request. The basic filing fee, search fee, examination fee, and any required excess claims and application size fees are filed with the request or have been already been paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All applicable fees must accompany the Track One request (or have already been paid). References to specific fee provisions: 37 CFR 1.17(i) (processing fee), 1.17(c) (prioritized examination fee), and 1.18(d) (publication fee). Ensure excess-claim and application-size fees are paid where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim-count and claim-type limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The application contains or is amended to contain no more than four independent claims and no more than thirty total claims, and no multiple dependent claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before or at the time of filing the Track One request, the application must meet these limits; if necessary, amend the claims to comply. Multiple dependent claims are not permitted for Track One.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original application eligibility and filing-route (Track One original filing)
rubrics_metrics.description: For Original Application (Track One) under § 1.102(e)(1): (a) The application is an original nonprovisional utility application filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) filed via EFS-Web, OR (b) the application is an original nonprovisional plant application filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) filed in paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the appropriate box for original utility vs plant applications. Utility original applications must be submitted via EFS-Web when filing this certification and request; plant originals are submitted in paper as indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oath or declaration requirement for original applications
rubrics_metrics.description: An executed oath or declaration under 37 CFR 1.63 is filed with the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When filing an original Track One application, ensure an executed oath/declaration meeting 37 CFR 1.63 is included with the application submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility conditions for Request for Continued Examination (RCE) Track One requests
rubrics_metrics.description: For Request for Continued Examination - Prioritized Examination under § 1.102(e)(2): (i) A request for continued examination has been filed with, or prior to, this form; (ii) If the application is a utility application, this certification and request is being filed via EFS-Web; (iii) The application is an original nonprovisional utility application filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a), or is a national stage entry under 35 U.S.C. 371; (iv) This certification and request is being filed prior to the mailing of a first Office action responsive to the request for continued examination; (v) No prior request for continued examination has been granted prioritized examination status under 37 CFR 1.102(e)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All five RCE-specific conditions must be satisfied to obtain Track One via an RCE: the RCE filing timing, filing route (EFS-Web for utilities), application type/status, timing relative to the first Office action responsive to the RCE, and that no prior RCE has already received Track One status. Ensure the RCE and this certification are timely and that the application class (original utility or national stage) is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signatures and representation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Signatures of all the inventors or assignees of record of the entire interest or their representative(s) are required in accordance with 37 CFR 1.33 and 11.18. See 37 CFR 1.4(d) for the form of the signature. If necessary, submit multiple forms for more than one signature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all required parties sign the certification as specified by the cited regulations. Include practitioner name, printed/typed name, date, and practitioner registration number where applicable. Use additional forms if multiple signatures are needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form submission metadata (number of forms)
rubrics_metrics.description: If multiple signatures are required, submit multiple forms as necessary and indicate the total number of forms submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide accurate accounting of how many certification forms are being submitted when multiple signature pages are needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy Act notice: voluntary furnishing and processing consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Furnishing of the information solicited is voluntary; the principal purpose for which the information is used by the USPTO is to process and/or examine your submission related to a patent application or patent. If you do not furnish the requested information, the USPTO may not be able to process and/or examine your submission, which may result in termination of proceedings or abandonment of the application or expiration of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should be aware that while provision of information is voluntary under the Privacy Act, failure to provide required information may prevent USPTO processing and could cause termination or abandonment. Provide the requested data to avoid adverse procedural consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy Act routine uses and possible disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Information provided will be treated confidentially to the extent allowed under FOIA and the Privacy Act, but records may be disclosed for routine uses including disclosure to the Department of Justice, contractors performing agency work, Members of Congress upon request involving an individual, the International Bureau of WIPO for PCT matters, other federal agencies for national security review, GSA during inspections, the public after publication or issuance (subject to limitations), and to law enforcement agencies if the USPTO becomes aware of violations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should understand the specific routine uses enumerated (1–9) describing circumstances in which USPTO may disclose records: to DOJ, in litigation, to congressional offices on constituent requests, contractors subject to confidentiality obligations, WIPO for PCT filings, for national security/Atomic Energy Act review, to GSA for record inspections, to the public after publication/issuance or under certain conditions for abandoned applications, and to law enforcement where appropriate. This is informational—no separate action required other than being aware of potential disclosures.
